newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end lower, feeders pare gains.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end lower, feeders pare gains.

text.p: CME live cattle futures slipped on selling prompted by lower boxed beef values at noon but finished with only small losses after trading higher early. Feeder cattle pared gains on fund selling, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.025 to 0.200 cent per lb lower with June off 0.050 at 64.125 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.200 to 0.100 higher with August up 0.150 at 77.300 cents.

Live cattle slipped late for small losses as selling on further weakness in boxed beef and late position squaring weighed on prices. But underlying support was still evident with prices in the 63 to 64 cent area, traders said.

The current price level of futures has been a long-term support area. Also, some traders cited the active feedlot movement which may indicate better than expected packer demand for fed cattle and possible good beef business, they said.
The Kansas weekly feedlot volume was a new record by 100 head at 136,500 head. The previous record was in the week ended Aug 22, 1996 at 136,400 head, USDA said.
"We moved a good number of cattle this week and caught up were we got behind last week," said Tom Tippens, CEO of Professional Cattle Consultants Inc.
Tippens thought the $64 level could hold into next week. Beef movement is expected to be larger than normal due to the favorable retail margin that beef holds to pork, he said.
"It's (Beef) still priced competitively with pork and there is obviously adequate supplies. It's a good market for them (retailers) to continue to feature."

E.D.&F. Man bought June late while Prudential Securities and locals sold. Refco notably bought June early. R.J. O'Brien bought August while ING sold. Prudential and Cargill Investor Services were early buyers in August while LIT division of First Options and Refco sold, pit sources said.

In live cattle options, there was liquidation in June with commission houses on both sides of the 64 straddle. Commercials were hedging in December by buying 68 puts and selling 72 calls. Scattered hedging was also cited in August and October, buying puts and selling calls, pit sources added.
Persistent fund selling clipped much of the gains in feeder cattle after running up early on support from lower corn futures and continued strength in the cash feeder market, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.32 to $77.74 per cwt, they highest level since August 19, 1994.
Some traders look for prices to remain strong despite a normal seasonal period of weakness that come in June and July.
"We are through most of our spring run and wheat pasture cattle have already moved. For awhile now it is going to be very, very tight - there's just not many cattle out there," Tippens said.
He noted there will be some cattle coming off grass in July, but it will be August or September before feeder runs pick up again.

Dean Witter actively sold August while locals bought against short sales in September. ABN Chicago Corp and Smith Barney were buyers in September. Cargill spread long August feeers/short February live cattle, pit sources said.
